evidence: count, locate and extract (LF- and psi-based) for csa_* in suffix_array_algorithm.hpp, any pattern length; csa_wt built on an 8.9e9-char text (paper). Generic, not DNA-specialised.
Patterns are plain character iterators (backward_search/forward_search/count/locate); no IUPAC, wildcard or character-class support in suffix_array_algorithm.hpp.
No approximate-search routine. Only primitives: single-char backward_search and bidirectional_search(_forward/_backward); backtracking or search schemes are user code.
No MEM/MUM/maximal-repeat routine. cst_sct3 exposes sl, wl, lca, child, depth and DFS iterators, so the algorithm must be written by the user on CST primitives.
No matching-statistics API; bidirectional_search only cites the MS paper and extends intervals. MS is user code on CST sl/child or backward_search.
No generalized-index class in include/. Document listing/top-k (SADA, GREEDY of Culpepper et al.) is composed from csa+wt+rmq in benchmark/document_retrieval, not a library API.
No reverse-complement handling in the headers; both strands requires the user to append the reverse complement to the text. bidirectional_search exists but is not strand-aware.
cst_sct3 public API: root, parent, sibling, child, select_child, degree, sl, wl, lca, depth, node_depth, lb/rb, leftmost_leaf, DFS and bottom-up iterators. Reference CST design.
Only H0 and Hk entropy helpers in suffix_tree_algorithm.hpp. LRS, distinct-substring counts, supermaximal repeats need user traversal of the CST.
csa_wt build on text (Xeon E5640, 2013): 100 MB 25-29 s, 1 GB 307-379 s, 8.5 GB 4482-5282 s = ~1.6-4 MB/s, sequential. Not DNA, no head-to-head.
CSA 5.3 bits/char incl. 2.4 bits of SA samples on ENWIKI text; word-SADA build 5250 s, peak 13 GB for 4.6 GB input. Tunable csa_wt<wt_huff<rrr_vector>>; no DNA figure.
No latency numbers published in the repo (benchmark/indexing_count|locate are code only). FM count is O(m log sigma) via wavelet-tree backward_search; no head-to-head published.
csa_wt built on ENWIKI-BIG, 8,945,231,276 chars (8.5 GB) in 4482-5282 s; README says 64-bit supported; construct_sa switches to divsufsort64 above 2^31. Text, not DNA.
Semi-external construction (construct_sa_se, int_vector_buffer; paper Sect. 3) but a built CSA/CST must be RAM-resident to query; int_vector_mapper maps plain vectors only.
construct_sa.hpp and construct_lcp.hpp contain no OpenMP or thread code; SA via sequential divsufsort/divsufsort64 (qsufsort for integer alphabets).
No thread-safety statement in README or cst_sct3.hpp; const queries only read. A global memory_manager/id-counter race (construction/destruction) was fixed in SDSL PR 126 per seqan3 issue 3389.
No dynamic CSA/CST/FM-index and no append or insert/delete of texts in include/sdsl; structures are static (only small helpers such as nn_dict_dynamic).
csa_wt<wt_huff<rrr_vector>> is Hk-compressed: 5.3 bits/char with samples vs 64-bit plain SA, ~12x smaller. No run-length or pangenome-scale index in the library.
byte_alphabet and int_alphabet strategies (integer/word alphabets, paper Sect. 2.3); alphabet compaction gives log-sigma wavelet depth. No explicit 2-bit DNA path documented.
Documented serialize/store_to_file/load_from_file (fm-index.cpp), cereal archives in v3; int_vector_mapper memory-maps plain vectors only; no format version or checksum.
Header-only C++20 templates (v3), no C ABI; a .NET route needs a hand-written C++/CLI or C wrapper per instantiated template type.
conda-forge (v2.1.1, GPL-3) and Fedora sdsl-lite-devel 3.0.3 (BSD-3); CMake/submodule install. No CLI, PyPI or NuGet package.
GitHub Actions: 7 compilers x cereal on/off, ASan job, ctest; googletest suites for csa, cst, wt, lcp/sa construction, bidirectional search. Oracle comparison not verified.
xxsds fork v3.0.4 released 2026-07-01, commits on 2026-11-02, 9 open issues, BSD-3-Clause. Upstream simongog v2.1.1 (2016) idle since 2019 (GPL-3).
search() gives count (O(1) cursor.count), locate and lazy_locate for any pattern length; no text extraction from the index (path_label needs the original text).
Queries must use the index alphabet; no IUPAC, wildcard or character-class matching in the search configuration or in the cursor API.
Optimum search schemes (Kianfar et al.) on bi_fm_index: Hamming and edit via max_error_total/substitution/insertion/deletion; schemes up to 3 errors, backtracking beyond.
No MEM/MUM/maximal-repeat API; bi_fm_index_cursor offers extend_left/right, cycle_back/front, count and locate only, so MEM finding is user code.
No matching-statistics API; user code on cursor extend_right/extend_left, with no suffix links so each anchor restarts.
Text-collection layout (text_layout::collection) returns a reference_id per hit; no k-common-substring, LCS or document-counting API.
No both-strand option in the search configuration or fm_index; user must search reverse-complemented queries or index reverse complements themselves.
Cursor API: extend_right/left, cycle_back/front, query_length (depth), count, path_label on an implicit suffix tree; no suffix links, parent, LCA or visitors.
No LRS, distinct-substring, k-mer statistics or repeat analytics in the search/fm_index modules (only search, count, locate).
Built by sdsl construct_im (sequential; fm_index.hpp TODO on external/algorithm choice). No SeqAn3 timing published; underlying sdsl csa_wt ~1.6-4 MB/s (2013 hardware).
Issue 2759: 1.2 GB collection needed ~12 GB RAM to build (~10 B/char, 3.1.0-rc.1). SA sampling 16; bi_fm_index ~2x fm_index. Final index size not published.
Only SeqAn2-era bidirectional timings: hg38, 100k 101-bp reads, Hamming K=1/2/3 = 7.4/18.8/68.7 s single thread (OSS paper). No SeqAn3 figures; exact count is O(m).
Multi-GB build bug fixed (PR 2756; 4.8 GB collection failed in 3.1.0-rc.1) but no documented human-genome/3 Gbp run; size_type comes from sdsl, width not stated.
Index is built in RAM via construct_im and loaded fully through cereal; no mmap or disk-resident mode in fm_index.hpp.
No parallel construction: fm_index.hpp calls sdsl construct_im with no threading; the 'parallel' configuration applies to search only.
search_cfg::parallel runs queries on N threads over one shared index, deterministic result order for the lazy range. Open issue 3389 concerns per-thread index create/destroy.
Static index only; no append or insert/delete of texts in the fm_index/bi_fm_index API.
fm_index is an sdsl csa_wt (BWT in wt_blcd, SA sample 16), far below an 8 B/char plain SA; bi_fm_index ~2x. No published ratio; no run-length variant.
Any semialphabet with <=256 ranks (static_assert), compact for dna4; no Unicode or integer alphabets; ranks 254/255 reserved as sentinels.
Documented cereal binary load/store; no mmap, format version or checksum; docs warn the default sdsl index type may change between releases.
C++20 header-only templates with no C ABI; .NET use needs a native wrapper.
Bioconda (3.4.2) and Debian libseqan3-dev (3.4.0) packages, CMake/CPM; no CLI or server tool surface.
README claims >97% unit-test coverage and performance regression tests; GitHub Actions CI; unit tests for search schemes, fm_index, cursors, configuration. Oracle comparison not verified.
Exact search via gt tagerator -e 0 on ESA or packed index (positions, strands) but tags are capped at 64 chars; text access via gt encseq decode; no general count/locate API.
No IUPAC/class patterns documented; IUB codes in the text never match (repfind manual). tagerator -withwildcards reports matches over N in the text only (not with -pck).
gt tagerator -e k: edit-distance search (cdiff/pdiff modes) over ESA or packed index, both strands, -best; tag length limited to 64 on 64-bit builds; CLI only.
gt repfind: all maximal forward and reversed repeats (pairs) with minimum length -l from a suffixerator ESA, also across sequences in the index; no MUM option documented.
gt matstat (-esa/-fmi/-pck, -query) and tagerator ms-mode report matching-statistics lengths and positions (-maxocc); tagerator tags limited to 64.
Multi-sequence ESA (separator table, seqnum in output); genomediff compares genomic units held in one index, uniquesub finds substrings unique across it; no k-common/LCS API.
suffixerator -mirrored virtually appends the reverse complement (genomediff manual); tagerator searches both strands by default (-nod/-nop); repfind -r/-p reverse-strand repeats.
ESA bottom-up lcp-interval traversal with visitors exists internally (src/match esa-bottomup-*.inc) and is not exposed as a documented public API.
tallymer (k-mer counts, occurrence ratios, unique/non-unique k-mer distributions), uniquesub (minimum unique substrings), repfind (maximal repeats), genomediff/shulengthdist (shustrings).
Measured 2008: human chr2 (243 Mbp) ESA built in ~5 min (~0.8 Mbp/s), 24 human chromosomes (~3000 Mb) ~1 h; whole-genome packed index 'little more than two hours' (tagerator manual).
Packed (FM) index of the whole human genome = 2.6 GB (~0.85 B/char, -locfreq 32). Plain ESA is 5n bytes (suftab+lcp); chr2 ESA build peak 1218.67 MB (~5 B/char).
No query-latency numbers published; genomediff manual says FM-index (packed) Kr computation 'takes significantly longer' than on the ESA. ESA lookups use mapped tables.
Manual builds a packed index of all 24 human chromosomes (-parts 12) = 2.6 GB .bdx; 64-bit executable via 'make 64bit=yes'. Also documented ESA of 3.2 GB ESTs (tallymer).
suffixerator -parts/-memlimit builds the ESA in bounded memory (3.2 GB ESTs 'works well'); -scan streams very large ESAs instead of mapping them (tallymer, repfind).
sfx-suffixer.c sorts buckets in threads when built with GT_THREADS_ENABLED and gt_jobs>1 (-lcp rejected with >1 thread); no speed-up numbers documented.
Index files are read-only and mappable by many processes; no thread-safety statement for the C library or tools; concurrency documented only for suffixerator bucket sorting.
ESA and packed index are static files produced by suffixerator/packedindex; no append, insert or delete is documented in any tool.
Packed index (FM) of the human genome is 2.6 GB vs ~12.4 GB for a plain 4-byte SA (~4.7x, assuming ~3.1 Gbp); no run-length/pangenome index; the ESA itself is uncompressed.
DNA, protein and user symbol maps (-smap), bit-compressed encseq (-sat bit...); wildcards stored as special ranges; no Unicode or integer alphabets documented.
Documented index files (.suf .lcp .bwt .tis .ssp .des .prj, packed .bdx), mapped on load (repfind default), suffixerator -md5 sums, chkintegrity tool; format spec/versioning not verified.
Primary surface is the CLI (gt suffixerator, repfind, ...); libgenometools C API documents GtEncseq etc. but no ESA/FM classes, so .NET use is CLI/process or a custom C wrapper.
CLI tools; Debian, Ubuntu, Homebrew and AUR packages (README badges); Python, Ruby, Lua and Go bindings in repo. No PyPI/NuGet, no server/MCP surface.
testsuite has suffixerator, repfind, packedindex, tallymer, genomediff, encseq tests; CI runs scripts/citest.rb on 18 Linux + 3 macOS jobs. Oracle comparison not verified.
